title: The Sheep in the Field
summary: Roderick Chisholm's case: you look into a field and see what looks exactly like a sheep, and so you believe there is a sheep in the field. What you are looking at is really a dog, disguised as a sheep. But there is a sheep in the field, out of sight behind a hill. Your belief is true, and you had every reason for it; but the thing that made it true had nothing to do with the thing you saw.
citations: Roderick Chisholm, Theory of Knowledge (Prentice-Hall, 1966; 2nd ed. 1977)
Edmund L. Gettier, "Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?", Analysis 23(6) (1963): 121–123
Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup, "The Analysis of Knowledge," Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/knowledge-analysis/
